corporeal|somatic.distinction: Corporeal means having a physical body at all, while somatic means relating to that body as opposed to the mind.

corroborate|substantiate.distinction: Corroborate adds a second source confirming an account, while substantiate supplies the evidence that establishes a claim.

cosmopolitan|universal.distinction: Cosmopolitan means at home among many cultures, while universal means applying to every case without exception.

countenance|sanction.distinction: Countenance tolerates or approves something, while sanction can either authorise it or punish it, depending on the sentence.

countermand|repeal.distinction: Countermand cancels an order already given, while repeal strikes a law off the books.

countermand|rescind.distinction: Countermand reverses a specific order, while rescind cancels a decision or grant more generally.

cower|fawn.distinction: Cower crouches away in fear, while fawn crawls toward someone with flattery.

cower|grovel.distinction: Cower shrinks back from a threat, while grovel abases itself to win favour.

cower|quail.distinction: Cower is the body crouching away from danger, while quail is the heart failing before it.

coy|demure.distinction: Coy is shyness put on to intrigue, while demure is genuine modesty of manner, though it too can be affected.

crafty|cunning.distinction: Crafty and cunning both mean skilled at deception; cunning is the sharper intelligence, crafty the readier trickery.

crafty|wily.distinction: Crafty is skilled at trickery, while wily is always a move ahead and hard to catch.

crevice|fissure.distinction: A crevice is a narrow crack you could put a finger in, while a fissure is a split that can run through rock or a party.

cryptic|inscrutable.distinction: Cryptic hides a meaning that could be decoded, while inscrutable gives nothing away to decode at all.

crystallize|elucidate.distinction: Crystallize is a vague idea taking definite form, while elucidate is making an existing idea clear to someone else.

cultured|genteel.distinction: Cultured means genuinely refined by education and taste, while genteel suggests refinement kept up for show.

cumbersome|inept.distinction: Cumbersome describes a thing too bulky to handle, while inept describes a person too clumsy to handle it.

cunning|guile.distinction: Cunning is the adjective for the clever deceiver, while guile is the noun for the deceit itself.

cunning|wily.distinction: Cunning and wily both mean cleverly deceptive; wily stresses the knack of always staying a step ahead.

cursory|perfunctory.distinction: Cursory means done too quickly to be thorough, while perfunctory means done only because it had to be done at all.

dais|podium.distinction: A dais is the raised platform a whole table or seat of honour stands on, while a podium is the small stand one speaker occupies.

dapper|natty.distinction: Dapper and natty both describe neat stylish dress; dapper suits the whole trim figure, natty the sharpness of the clothes.

dapper|raffish.distinction: Dapper is neat and correct in dress, while raffish is stylish in a slightly disreputable way.

dapper|rakish.distinction: Dapper is trim and impeccable, while rakish wears the same clothes at a careless angle and looks faintly scandalous.

debase|demoralize.distinction: Debase lowers the quality or worth of something, while demoralize destroys the confidence of a person.

debase|deprave.distinction: Debase reduces value or dignity, while deprave corrupts morals outright.

decimate|eradicate.distinction: Decimate destroys a large part of something, while eradicate leaves nothing of it at all.

decorous|seemly.distinction: Decorous and seemly both mean fitting and proper; decorous stresses dignity, seemly stresses what the occasion allows.

decorum|propriety.distinction: Decorum is dignified conduct suited to an occasion, while propriety is conformity to the accepted standards generally.

decree|edict.distinction: A decree is any authoritative order with legal force, while an edict is one proclaimed by a ruler or sovereign body.

decry|excoriate.distinction: Decry denounces something publicly, while excoriate attacks it so harshly the criticism draws blood.

decry|objurgate.distinction: Decry condemns a practice in public, while objurgate scolds a particular person to their face.

deduce|derive.distinction: Deduce reaches a conclusion by reasoning, while derive traces something back to the source it came from.

deduce|infer.distinction: Deduce follows necessarily from the premises, while infer draws a likely conclusion from evidence that could point elsewhere.

deflect|parry.distinction: Deflect turns something aside in any way, while parry is the trained blocking motion of a fencer or a politician.

degrade|demean.distinction: Degrade lowers the quality or rank of something, while demean lowers a person in dignity.

deject|demoralize.distinction: Deject lowers someone's spirits for a time, while demoralize destroys their will to keep going.

delimit|delineate.distinction: Delimit sets the boundaries of something, while delineate draws out what lies inside them in detail.

demoralize|deprave.distinction: Demoralize breaks a person's confidence, while deprave corrupts their morals.

denigrate|slander.distinction: Denigrate blackens a reputation by unfair criticism, while slander is the spoken falsehood that a court can act on.

denounce|stigmatize.distinction: Denounce attacks someone publicly on one occasion, while stigmatize attaches a lasting mark of disgrace.

derelict|dilapidated.distinction: Derelict means abandoned, and of a person negligent in duty, while dilapidated describes the physical disrepair itself.

derive|infer.distinction: Derive traces something back to its source, while infer reasons forward from evidence to a conclusion.

despite|disdain.distinction: Despite is the older noun for contempt and spite, while disdain is the haughty scorn that refuses to stoop.

despite|scorn.distinction: Despite survives chiefly in set phrases, while scorn is the everyday word for contempt openly shown.

despoil|pillage.distinction: Despoil strips a place of what made it valuable, while pillage is the violent looting of it, usually in war.

despotic|dictatorial.distinction: Despotic describes absolute oppressive power held, while dictatorial describes the domineering manner of someone wielding it.

destitute|indigent.distinction: Destitute and indigent both mean desperately poor; destitute stresses having nothing left, indigent the settled condition of want.

detachment|insularity.distinction: Detachment is standing back to judge impartially, while insularity is being cut off and unable to see beyond one's own circle.

detente|rapprochement.distinction: Detente is the easing of hostility between rivals, while rapprochement is the friendly relations actually restored.

deviate|digress.distinction: Deviate departs from an established course, while digress wanders off the subject and usually comes back.

diaphanous|gossamer.distinction: Diaphanous stresses that light passes through the fabric, while gossamer stresses how impossibly fine and light it is.

dictatorial|overbearing.distinction: Dictatorial is authority exercised absolutely, while overbearing is a manner that crushes others whether or not the authority exists.

differentiate|discriminate.distinction: Differentiate tells two things apart neutrally, while discriminate can also mean treating one of them unfairly.

dilate|elaborate.distinction: Dilate widens something, and in speech means to go on at length, while elaborate describes intricate detailed design.

dilate|expatiate.distinction: Dilate on a subject and expatiate on it both mean speaking at length; dilate also keeps its physical sense of widening.

dilate|expound.distinction: Dilate on a topic is to dwell on it at length, while expound is to set it out and explain it systematically.

dilatory|laggard.distinction: Dilatory describes the habit of delaying, while a laggard is the person who has fallen behind the rest.

diligent|industrious.distinction: Diligent is careful steady attention to the work, while industrious is the sheer quantity of work done.

dingy|disconsolate.distinction: A dingy room is dirty and depressing to look at, while a disconsolate person is the one sitting in it beyond comforting.

din|tumult.distinction: A din is loud continuous noise, while a tumult is noisy disorder with confusion and movement in it.

dirge|elegy.distinction: A dirge is sung at the graveside, an elegy is written and read; the dirge is music, the elegy is verse.

disaffected|malcontent.distinction: Disaffected describes loyalty that has curdled, while a malcontent is the person who has been complaining all along.

discomfit|disconcert.distinction: To discomfit someone is to leave them embarrassed and at a loss, while to disconcert them is to throw their composure off for a moment.

discount|dismiss.distinction: You discount evidence by giving it less weight than it deserves, and dismiss it by refusing to weigh it at all.

discount|disregard.distinction: To discount a claim is to count it for less, while to disregard it is to act as though it had never been made.

discrepancy|variance.distinction: A discrepancy is two figures that ought to match and do not, while a variance is the measured size of the gap between them.

discriminating|incisive.distinction: A discriminating palate tells fine things apart, while an incisive question cuts to the heart of a matter in one stroke.

discriminating|keen.distinction: Discriminating taste notices fine differences, while a keen eye simply misses nothing; one sorts, the other spots.

disdain|scorn.distinction: Disdain looks down in cold silence, while scorn says so out loud; disdain withholds respect, scorn actively mocks.

disinterested|impartial.distinction: A disinterested judge has nothing to gain from the outcome, while an impartial one shows no favour whichever way they lean.

dismiss|disregard.distinction: To dismiss a proposal is to reject it outright, while to disregard it is to leave it lying unanswered.

disperse|dissipate.distinction: A crowd disperses when it scatters in all directions, while a fortune dissipates when it scatters until nothing is left.

disport|gambol.distinction: To disport oneself is to take pleasure at leisure, while to gambol is to skip and leap like a lamb in a field.

disregard|snub.distinction: To disregard someone is simply not to notice them, while to snub them is to make the not noticing unmistakable.

dissembler|phony.distinction: A dissembler hides real motives behind a convincing front, while a phony has no substance behind the front at all.

dissemble|feign.distinction: To dissemble is to hide the feeling you actually have, while to feign is to display a feeling you do not have.

dissident|heretical.distinction: A dissident is a person who opposes the official line, while heretical describes the belief itself as against doctrine.

dissident|heterodox.distinction: A dissident opposes the authorities openly, while heterodox describes an opinion that simply departs from the accepted one.

distort|garble.distinction: To distort a message is to bend its meaning on purpose, while to garble it is to scramble it so no meaning survives.

dogged|pertinacious.distinction: Dogged persistence is admired for its endurance, while pertinacious persistence irritates because it will not let go.

dogged|tenacious.distinction: Dogged effort keeps plodding forward, while a tenacious grip simply refuses to release what it already holds.

dolorous|lachrymose.distinction: Dolorous describes grief in the voice or the scene, while lachrymose describes the tears, whether shed or provoked.

dulcet|mellifluous.distinction: Dulcet tones are sweet and soothing to hear, while mellifluous ones flow smoothly like honey; sweetness against smoothness.

ebullient|exuberant.distinction: Ebullient spirits bubble up in the moment, while exuberant energy grows and spills over abundantly.

eclipse|overshadow.distinction: To eclipse a rival is to surpass them outright, while to overshadow them is to loom so large they go unnoticed.

economical|frugal.distinction: An economical method wastes nothing, while a frugal person chooses to spend little; one is efficient, the other abstemious.

economical|sparing.distinction: Economical use gets full value from what is spent, while sparing use simply parts with as little as possible.

economical|stinting.distinction: An economical budget avoids waste, while a stinting one grudges what it hands over; the first is prudent, the second mean.

effervescent|scintillating.distinction: An effervescent manner bubbles with cheerful energy, while scintillating talk sparkles with cleverness.

effrontery|gall.distinction: Effrontery is shameless boldness with a formal ring, while gall is the same nerve described with contempt.

effrontery|presumption.distinction: Effrontery is brazen and knows it, while presumption is the quieter arrogance of assuming a right one does not have.

egregious|flagrant.distinction: An egregious error stands out for how bad it is, while a flagrant one stands out for being committed openly.

elaborate|expatiate.distinction: Elaborate describes a design worked out in fine detail, while to expatiate is to go on at length about a subject.

elaborate|expound.distinction: An elaborate plan is intricate in its construction, while to expound a plan is to set it out at length for an audience.

elated|jubilant.distinction: Elated describes spirits lifted high by good news, while jubilant adds the triumph and the noise of celebration.

elicit|evoke.distinction: You elicit an answer by asking for it, while a smell evokes a memory without anyone asking anything.

elicit|kindle.distinction: To elicit a response is to draw it out of someone, while to kindle interest is to set it alight where there was none.

elicit|provoke.distinction: To elicit a reaction is to draw it out deliberately, while to provoke one is to goad until it bursts out.

eloquent|facile.distinction: Eloquent speech is fluent and moves people, while facile speech is fluent and has nothing underneath it.
